text:
maria: quick heads-up — ran a focused comparison between bitsandbytes int8 and llm.int8 on long-context slices (2k-8k) and wanted to capture weird failure modes i saw :thinking_face:

sam: nice, what metrics?

maria: EM/ExactMatch on QA eval, BLEU/ROUGE for summarization, plus p95 latency and jitter under 128 concurrent reqs. also tracked token-level divergence (per-token logprob drift)

jess: did you use our standard priming prompts or the longer multi-turn simulated user traces?

maria: multi-turn traces — mixing priming + followups, we saw two clear regimes: up to ~2048 tokens bnb-int8 maintains parity with llm.int8; beyond that llm.int8 shows fewer hallucination spikes but slightly worse latency. bnb has lower p95 but increased token-delta after 3k tokens.

kai: can you paste the exact commands/flags you used? might try on A/B nodes

maria: sure — ran on dedicated staging pool (A100s), simplified script:

```bash
./run_eval.sh --model-ref huggingface/aurora13b --quant bnb-8bit --ctx 4096 --batch 1 --trace outputs/bnb-4096.log
./run_eval.sh --model-ref huggingface/aurora13b --quant llmint8 --ctx 4096 --batch 1 --trace outputs/llmint8-4096.log
```

maria: key flags: --prefetch_kv true, --kv-cache-policy rolling(512), --token-prime 32

sam: what did the EM delta look like? numbers?

maria: for QA slices (N=1k examples): EM delta (bnb - llm.int8) = -0.8% at 2k ctx, -1.5% at 4k ctx, -3.9% at 8k ctx. but p95 latency bnb was ~12% lower at 4k ctx.

jess: interesting. so bnb trades a bit of quality for latency at very long contexts. any pattern in where it goes wrong?

maria: mostly reduced context carryover — model forgets earlier disambiguating facts more often. token-logprob drift analysis shows bnb has increasing negative drift after 2500 tokens (avg -0.06 per token vs -0.02 for llm.int8)

kai: did you test AWQ or GPTQ variants too?

maria: quick AWQ run on 4k showed similar quality to llm.int8 but latency closer to bnb; GPTQ not applicable for this model (decoder-only weights shape mismatch).

sam: any hypothesis on root cause? kernel-level accumulation error? activation scaling?

maria: my current guess: weight-only quant rounding combined with attention key/value scaling interacting with rolling KV policy. bnb's fast path favors lower-precision matmul kernels which slightly amplify small numerical errors across long recurrences.

jess: ops question — if we ship bnb for Dedicated, is it safe to route short-context traffic to it and keep long-context on llm.int8?

maria: that's my recommendation. routing policy prototype:

```json
{"route_rules": [{"max_context_tokens": 2048, "model_variant": "bnb-8bit"}, {"min_context_tokens": 2049, "model_variant": "llmint8"}], "fallback": "llmint8"}
```

maria: also suggest a canary that measures per-slice EM and token-drift for first 48h before full promotion

kai: what about batching and burst behavior? any interaction?

maria: yes — bnb's latency advantage shrinks with larger batch sizes; at batch=8 the p95 delta is ~2-3% in bnb's favor (versus 12% at batch=1). when we enable continuous batching (svc-default) the divergence in quality remains — it's not a batching artifact.

sam: got it. also need an ops playbook for fallbacks if we see quality regressions mid-rollout

maria: proposed rollout steps: 1) small canary 1% traffic short-context bnb, 2) 24h metric gating on EM/token-drift/p95, 3) 10% short-ctx, 4) monitor and hold, 5) widen to 50% then long-ctx only on llm.int8. include automated rollback threshold: EM drop >1.5% or token-drift mean >-0.03.

jess: could you upload the raw traces and diff plots to the shared eval dashboard? i'll add them to the model-card notes

maria: uploaded logs and token-drift plots to /evals/aurora13b/quant_longseq/ — added short summary in the dashboard.

deploy-bot: deploy suggestion created: quant-canary-bnb-shortctx -> target:fleet-staging, schedule: immediate, rollback: disabled=false

sam: OK let's run the canary tomorrow 09:00 PST, i'll standby for observability hooks

maria: thanks all — i'll draft a small blurb for the release notes explaining the routing recommendation and the EM tradeoffs

jess: :thumbsup:
